meta_description_ru: Письма читателей журнала Outlet №16 (часть 1): группа пользователей INDUG, адаптация Tasword, подключение Interface 1 и Microdrive к ZX Spectrum +3.
body_en_plain:
Christmas, 1988      Page  Reply

 How to write to us...02     -
 Trevor Wright........03    05
 G.A. Matthews........06    06
 Brian Gaff...........07    11
 John Luby............12    17
 Alan Rutherford......18     -
 Andrew Clapham.......20    21
 K.A. Schimmell.......23    24
 Nick Lewis...........25    26
 Kenneth B. Hunter....28    30
 Dave Cowling.........37    37

      HOW TO WRITE TO OUTLET
      ----------------------
Letters are accepted  in  almost
any form for publication in our
OUTLETTERS: BASIC PRINT or  DATA
statements, handwritten or typed
pages, a simple  JOTTER  program
is provided in Issue 2(Disk #4);
mailbox messages via Prestel No.
014703943 but the easiest for us
to edit are Tasword 2 files with
the right-hand margin set at 32.

Please state if there should  be
parts of your letter you do  not
wish published but we always use
our discretion  anyway.  Letters
may also be edited  for  clarity
and length... Please ask if  you
welcome  direct   correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From Trevor Wright, Leics.

Dear Ron,

One item of news which might
interest Tasword 128/+2 users is
that INDUG, the user group of
Disciple and +D users, has just
announced a conversion program
for Tasword 128/+2 which auto-
matically converts it for use
with the relevant interface. The
price is a mere `3.95, but this
will presumably be the price for
members. Whether others can
purchase it I'm not sure.

They also hope to announce a
conversion for Tasword +3 before
Christmas. How one converts this
to disc when it only comes on

microdrive cartridge I'm not
quite sure or why one should if
you already have microdrives but
I shall await the news with
interest as this is the version
I should like as I'm limited to
48K !
             Yours,

          Trevor Wright

To: Trevor Wright from Brian

Ah!The mysterious secret society
of INDUG! We'd be interested in
anything else you can tell us
about its activity and services.
Do they issue a newsletter? Do
you have any contact with other
users through the group, e.g.
through a letters' page? If so,
we'd be grateful if you could
draw their attention to OUTLET
as there is precious little
other software available on the
Disciple/+D format. Ron did try
more than once to join the group
but without any reply.How DO you
get to join? We heard the person
running the group never answers
his mail! (Sort of an anti-user
group!)                  - Brian

From: G.A. Matthews,  Barking

         ... If anyone has got a
microdrive to work on a Plus 3,
I would be very interested to
know how.

Brian Gaff has had some success
(see next outletter). I don't
know if he can help but write in
if you want to get in touch.

MGT may also be able to help.
Their "two-face" connector could
have been modified now to work
with the new +2A which has the
same circuit board as the +3.
Give them a ring on 0792 791100
or write Lakeside, Pheonix Way,
Swansea Enterprise Park, Swansea
SA7 9EH
                   - Brian

From Brian Gaff,  Surrey

Hi there again! I had better
clear up the +3 business [rumour
on the grapevine that "someone"
had got a microdrive working on
a +3!- B.C.]

What I have done is to wire a
small circuit on an edge card
and plug it into a short ribbon
cable. I then plug the edge card
into IF1 and the other end of
the ribbon into the + 3. This
gives me a 48K Speccy with IF 1.
It won't work in +3 mode though.
Other interfaces and add-ons
that will work with the circuit
are: Multiface 1/+D disc/VTX5000
Swiftdisc II. I feel sure others
will too. In the +D's case it is

important to keep the ribbon
very short or it can get
confused. I hope that a Twoface
can be used to isolate the
system to use +3 mode. Have you
got a +3 then?

This brings me to another query
that came up. There are Tas 3 to
Tas 2 convertors. I have one
here. I do not know its origins
but I will put a copy on here
for evaluation.

On the subject of tape to drive
conversions. You can use the one
I did some time back that is on
The Gnome BB if you want. It's
for Scrabble and is a complete
kit of programs so any foo..er
person can do it! However, it

only works on the later silver
label version of the game.

The next point is one of a
cautious nature! If you have
been twiddling your Microdrive
speed you will probably damage
the data on existing FORMATed
carts by recording on them. Be
careful! Next a mini Review for
+D owners.

PICK-POKE-IT is not some kind of
disease,it is the latest release
from MGT . It is a hard program
to categorise really as it both
gives the Snapshot a friendly
front end and contains many nice
programming tools.

It has a full disassembler,

Memory contents dump, a search
RAM function and the ability to
alter bytes and either go back
to the program or Re-snapshot
it. It is fully menu driven and
fairly easy to use. You can eas-
ily alter text in running games
and POKE the so called Multiface
pokes for infinite lives etc.The
only criticisms I had were that
the key repeat on some prompts
was too fast and kept meaning I
had to abort and restart and
that there was no way out to
save the program other than the
Snapshot. At around `14 it is
rather expensive but probably
worth it.

                  - Brian Gaff

To Brian Gaff from Brian

No, we've not got a +3 but if we
ever get one we'd certainly find
some sort of twoface useful to
transfer files from microdrive.

Hold the SCRABBLE convertor for
the moment but if anyone else is
interested please shout.

Thanks for the other info. Funny
about the key repeats. I myself
now find the standard Spectrum
repeat speed infuriatingly slow!
I usually POKE 23561,10 and POKE
23562,3 while programming and am
now so used to that pace that in
"normal mode" it seems like I've
time to make coffee while I'm
waiting for the key repeat! What
do others think?      - Brian

from:  John Luby, DUNS,

Dear Ron/Brian,

There's a slight bug in SPECLIST
[Issue 13] which seems to be my
fault. Entering STOP during the
search key input results in a
"variable not found" message, if
the printer flag PR has not yet
been initialised.Simply putting:
LET pr=i in line 100 solves the
problem. It doesn't seem to
matter how often you run a pro-
gram yourself you can bet bugs
appear when other people use it!
[You can say that again! - BC.]
It doesn't seem to matter how
often you run a program yourself
you can bet...[Oh shut up!]
There's a moral there somewhere.

Thanks for the offer to include
a GP100A routine in the text
reader, but I've already
extracted the core from your
text reader, and used it in a
program of my own with a printer
driver and text dump. If I want
hard copy I just load this
instead of CONTENTS. Certainly
not worth publishing, but if
anyone wants a copy let me know.

I'm surprised to hear how small
the readership is. It's got to
be the best Spectrum magazine
around, if only because it's the
ONLY magazine as far as anyone
serious about their Spectrum is
concerned.It can't be the price.
Short of giving it away free, I
can't see how Outlet could be


any cheaper.Continuing good luck
anyway. I'd be devastated to see
Outlet go the way of ZX Comput-
ing and 16/48.

All I can say about my spelling
clanger is "touche" (and even
that doesn't look right without
the accent!). If you promise not
to remind me of "competant"
again I won't mention your
"excercise" or "conjuction"!
Serves me rite for being pompus.
The American politician/cowboy/
philosopher Will Rogers once
said that it isn't the things we
DON'T know that cause trouble,
it's the things we DO know that
ain't so!

On the subject of letters, have


you thought of incorporating
HANDYWIDE into your text reader?
I suspect it might not be all
that easy, but you could get
more text onto a page.

I meant to mention in my last
letter (but forgot) how much I
enjoyed FONTOGRAPH by Drew
Turpin. Apart from the selection
of fonts (I have dozens, but can
never resist a few more),I think
the program is a very nice
example of neat, logical pro-
gramming. The author has taken a
simple idea(no offence intended,
Drew)and presented it in a neat,
original and attractive way.
Anyone thinking of trying their
hand at writing programs could
do worse than look inside this

one. And if that menu routine
gets hijacked by other contri-
butors, you WILL take it as a
compliment, won't you, Drew?

Any prizes HAVE to go, however,
to Issue 14's article on adapt-
ing the OPD microdrives! Now
THAT'S what I buy magazines for!
More of that kind of thing,
PLEASE! The same firm, J.T.Bull,
also sells small monitors, etc.,
but I haven't the expertise (or
the bottle!) to tinker. The idea
of an 8 inch monitor for under
`2O IS tempting, though.

Cheers,

John Luby.

To: John Luby from Brian

Thanks, John. Growth in OUTLET's
readership has been very slow as
we exhausted our own savings and
couldn't afford large promotion.
A small loan and modest adverts
are paying off a little now and
we've just had our best month to
date. One thing that's kept us
going is the high proportion of
contributed programs considering
the number of readers and the
enthusiasm voiced so frequently
by so many. Thanks to all.

(Places violin quietly on side
table - exits, head high, eyes
shining, to the left of stage)

From:Alan Rutherford,Farnborough

Dear Brian and Ron,

May I say how much I enjoy your
magazine? I am not sure if that
is the correct name for a disk
or cartridge-based information
and news system (bit long-winded
that),so I'll stick to magazine.

Please could you put a plea for
help in the listing? My printer
is a Seikosha GP-505. This needs
a paper roll 5 inches wide. I
woder if there is somebody out
there that knows if there is a
supplier of rolls of paper of
that size? Tandy do one that is
4.5 inches wide which will do
but like most Tandy goods is
greatly over-priced.

I don't know whether my set up
will interest you.It consists of
1. 48K Spectrum (series 3)
2. Fuller keyboard (this has
   never given any trouble)
3. Opus disk drive (drive 1 - 40
   track, drive 2 - 80 track
   single-sided)
4. RGB output unit and a Thorn
   Monitor T.V. which accepts
   RGB input or composite input.

I have another Spectrum which I
use with my microdrive but that
is always going for repair so
the microdrive does not get used
very much. I prefer disk anyway.

         Your sincerely,

         Alan Rutherford

From Andrew Clapham, Nottingham

Dear Ron & Brian,

Ref. your keyboard queries,I've
seen the "Digit" upgrade advert-
ised in the "brash" hypermarket
section for `7 for a couple of
months. Having both the 48K+ and
128K Spectrums I'd be interested
to hear if anyone has used them
and if they're worth getting.

I'd be interested in your custom
items for Tasword 2.Having man-
ged to load in minichars 2 and
get it to work first time and
having unglued a cartridge with
the OUT 239,252 tip one forgets
all the frustrations...
                  Many thanks,
                - Andrew Clapham

To Andrew Clapham from Brian

Others have also shown interest
in an improved Tasword 2 BASIC
so I think I WILL probably put a
new version in a future OUTLET.

We'll let you know if we can do
anything with the programming
problem you sent in, Andrew but
I suspect it may be too lengthy
a task in which to get involved.
If it were possible to include
it in OUTLET we could justify
the time spent but as it's a
copyrighted program.. Generally,
if anyone has a program needing
improvements or adjustments or
even if they want a complete
program writing for a particular
task, write in with as much

detail as possible and we'll see
what we can do. Obviously there
are projects too large or beyond
our skills but any reasonable
ideas we'll add to our projects
list. The only stipulation is
that it be freely shared with
other OUTLET readers. We cannot
spend too much time on private
help (much as we'd like to!).

                        - Brian

From: K.A. Schimmel, Nottingham

Gentlemen,

A reader asked how to use the
HR5 printer in 128 mode. This is
quite simple. Just increase the
baud rate to 9600 and the
printer will work with the built
in RS232 port not unlike an old
ZX Printer. Even Tasword 2 will
work except one can't send
control codes and it is best to
start with line 2 as, if one by
accident tries to go to line 0,
the computer will crash.

I am looking forward to more
OUTCLASS on machine code. I find
most books fairly useless as
they are all set to give you a

hexloader to type in plus a
program with a lot of WAFFLE
which leaves one bewildered.Well
at 64 anyway!

Last but not least, thanks for a
mag with a difference. I am one
of those who misses ZX COMPUTING
and still suffer from withdrawal
symptoms but OUTLET helps.

        Yours faithfully,

         K.A. Schimmell

Thanks for the info and glad to
hear you are enjoying OUTLET. I
wish we could get ALL the ex- ZX
COMPUTING readers to try our
magazine.
                        - Ron

From Nick Lewis, Cardiff


Dear Ron,

I am hoping to buy a printer in
the near future and I was
wondering if you could recommend
a cheap but reliable one. Also I
will need a suitable interface.

        Yours faithfully,

           Nick Lewis

To Nick Lewis from Brian

Quite good printers are now
available for under `200. The
CITIZEN 120D at `139.95 and the
STAR LC-10 at `199.95 are quite
popular. Both are available from
MGT, Lakeside, Phoenix Way,
Swansea Enterprise Park, Swansea
SA7 9EH. However for a real
bargain try a couple of older
BROTHER machines: the M1009 (the
machine I use all the time) now
available at only `114.05 or the
HR5 at an amazing `55.95 both
from UK HOME COMPUTERS, 82
Churchward Avenue, Swindon,Wilts
(Tel:0793 695034). All the above
print reasonable quality text or
graphics. All will work with a
Centronics type interface and I

suggest you get the Kempston E.,
`31.96 from W.A.V.E.,1 Buccleuch
Street,Barrow-in-Furness,Cumbria
LA14 1SR (Tel:0229 870000)unless
you're planning to get a drive
system like Disciple, +D, Opus
or microdrives in the future as
they all come with their own
printer interfaces built-in. If
you go for anything other than I
have suggested, check before you
part with your money that it
works with whatever interface
you get as there are two types:
Centronics or RS232.The Kempston
E is a Centronics interface.Most
printers are Centronics. Beware
some of the cheaper printer
interfaces needing software to
be loaded every time used (which
must be a flamin' nuisance!)
                         - Brian

From: Kenneth B. Hunter, N.Yorks

Dear Mr. Cavers,

There are a couple of problems
with which I would like help.

The first problem is in relation
to making a printout from the
pages of OUTLET which I have
been unable to do. I have a
Spectrum +2 with a Brother M1109
printer.The printer is connected
to the computer by a QL connect-
or cable (QPL-1) via the RS232/
Midi port. This works only in
128K mode but even when I run
OUTLET in 128K mode it does not
respond when I choose the Print
option. Is there a way round
this?

The second problem which I have
is, how does one SAVE a routine
from OUTLET to use in one's own
programs?

        Yours sincerely,

         Kenneth B. Hunter

To Kenneth Hunter from Brian

You can usually SAVE any whole
program from OUTLET by entering
RUN 9982 (Using RUN rather than
GO TO clears out any variables
and saves space on your drive).
You should check the line first
though on existing programs as
occasionally I have had to use a
different line (often 8982) for
various reasons. However, I am
now striving to make 9982 the
standard and 9983 for cassette
tape. 9980 has an ERASE option
for anyone wishing to ERASE an
earlier version first. I do NOT
normally recommend that you re-
SAVE on to your OUTLET disk or
cartridge but make a new working
copy (unless you've made a full
back-up of the whole OUTLET!)

Individual routines that are
actually described in a program
can almost always be extracted
in the following way:

Press E to ERASE the rest of
BASIC at the title page.

Enter SAVE etc...  "ANYNAME"
(do NOT add an auto-start line
number after the name)

LOAD your own program in which
you wish to use the routine.

Enter MERGE etc...  "ANYNAME"

Then follow the instructions
from the OUTLET program but it
will often just be GO SUB 1234
(or whatever line number is

given). This GO SUB instruction
should usually be entered in a
line near the beginning (after
loading) of your program. Always
follow the instructions in the
OUTLET program. Often, in the
case of CODE stored in REM
statements you will need to put
a CLEAR statement in the program
BEFORE the GO SUB to move RAMTOP
below the starting address of
the CODE. Test the program works
alright and then re-SAVE it.

To use a routine that happens
just to be in an OUTLET program,
i.e. not the main subject of the
program, you will need to delete
the rest of the BASIC either
line by line (!) or with a block
delete routine. (There is one
called DELINER in Issue 5).

Please write in if you have any
specific problems.

I am at present trying to
rationalize and standardize the
printer options used in OUTLET.
It is impossible to provide for
every interface so we cover the
main ones and I want to include
a "USER'S OWN" so anyone can
MERGE in their own routine. I am
trying to keep to the same line
numbers each time but it is not
easy.

Generally,you will need to BREAK
in to the program and LIST round
9700 to 9800 and alter one of
the existing interface set-up
lines to suit your system. In
most programs, line 9888 (which

at present is LPRINT III) will
initialize the printer for text
and 9895 will have any initial
control codes such as margin
settings. For high-res graphics
dumps look at 9782 and about
9786. The CONTENTS BASIC (also
TEXT LOADER for cassette users)
is different at present. Look at
line 1356. To save space the
codes are "embedded" in a string
in this line but just delete and
put your own codes in. Hopefully
I will standardize the CONTENTS
in line with other OUTLET
programs but at the moment I am
still collecting information.
One problem is that some
printers need a line feed code
and some don't. Another is that
the CONTENTS text may be totally
re-written.

In your particular case,I'm told
you have to initialize your
printer interface with:

FORMAT "P"; 1200 (or whatever
                  baud rate your
                  printer is set
                  at)
OPEN #3;"P"

POKE 23349,39: POKE 23350,1
  (before sending control codes)

You will probably need to exper-
iment a little to get things to
work but write in again with any
specific programs you have
trouble with. Sorry I can't be
more helpful but every program
is individual and may vary
slightly and also, I do not have


the +2 so can't try anything out
to be sure. Other OUTLET readers
using the +2 may be able to
advise you better so write again
if you get stuck.

                         - Brian.

From Dave Cowling, Leeds

Dear R & B,

Many thanks for the "minichars2"
font in issue No. 14, I have now
installed it in Tasword +2 (128
version) and find it a relaxing
font to work with.

For the benefit of any of your
readers who have not been able
to install the font (set up for
Tasword II), load as follows:-

LOAD*"m";1;"minichars2"CODE XXXX

where xxxx = 54528 for Tasword+2
and 38400 for Tasword 3.
                 - Dave Cowling.

Thanks, Dave. - Brian.

To Kenneth Hunter from Brian

You can usually SAVE any whole program from OUTLET by entering RUN 9982 (Using RUN rather than GO TO clears out any variables and saves space on your drive). You should check the line first though on existing programs as occasionally I have had to use a different line (often 8982) for various reasons. However, I am now striving to make 9982 the standard and 9983 for cassette tape. 9980 has an ERASE option for anyone wishing to ERASE an earlier version first. I do NOT normally recommend that you re- SAVE on to your OUTLET disk or cartridge but make a new working copy (unless you've made a full back-up of the whole OUTLET!)

Individual routines that are actually described in a program can almost always be extracted in the following way:

Press E to ERASE the rest of BASIC at the title page.

Enter SAVE etc...  "ANYNAME" (do NOT add an auto-start line number after the name)

LOAD your own program in which you wish to use the routine.

Enter MERGE etc...  "ANYNAME"

Then follow the instructions from the OUTLET program but it will often just be GO SUB 1234 (or whatever line number is

given). This GO SUB instruction should usually be entered in a line near the beginning (after loading) of your program. Always follow the instructions in the OUTLET program. Often, in the case of CODE stored in REM statements you will need to put a CLEAR statement in the program BEFORE the GO SUB to move RAMTOP below the starting address of the CODE. Test the program works alright and then re-SAVE it.

To use a routine that happens just to be in an OUTLET program, i.e. not the main subject of the program, you will need to delete the rest of the BASIC either line by line (!) or with a block delete routine. (There is one called DELINER in Issue 5).

Please write in if you have any specific problems.

I am at present trying to rationalize and standardize the printer options used in OUTLET. It is impossible to provide for every interface so we cover the main ones and I want to include a "USER'S OWN" so anyone can MERGE in their own routine. I am trying to keep to the same line numbers each time but it is not easy.

Generally,you will need to BREAK in to the program and LIST round 9700 to 9800 and alter one of the existing interface set-up lines to suit your system. In most programs, line 9888 (which

at present is LPRINT III) will initialize the printer for text and 9895 will have any initial control codes such as margin settings. For high-res graphics dumps look at 9782 and about 9786. The CONTENTS BASIC (also TEXT LOADER for cassette users) is different at present. Look at line 1356. To save space the codes are "embedded" in a string in this line but just delete and put your own codes in. Hopefully I will standardize the CONTENTS in line with other OUTLET programs but at the moment I am still collecting information. One problem is that some printers need a line feed code and some don't. Another is that the CONTENTS text may be totally re-written.

In your particular case,I'm told you have to initialize your printer interface with:

FORMAT "P"; 1200 (or whatever baud rate your printer is set

```text
                  at)
```

OPEN #3;"P"

POKE 23349,39: POKE 23350,1 (before sending control codes)

You will probably need to exper- iment a little to get things to work but write in again with any specific programs you have trouble with. Sorry I can't be more helpful but every program is individual and may vary slightly and also, I do not have

the +2 so can't try anything out to be sure. Other OUTLET readers using the +2 may be able to advise you better so write again if you get stuck.

## Как написать в OUTLET

Письма для публикации в нашей рубрике OUTLETTERS принимаются практически в любом виде: операторы PRINT или DATA в BASIC, рукописные или напечатанные на машинке страницы; простая программа JOTTER прилагается в Выпуске 2 (Disk #4); сообщения на почтовый ящик через Prestel № 014703943. Однако проще всего нам редактировать файлы Tasword 2 с правым полем, установленным на 32 колонки.

Пожалуйста, указывайте, если какие-то части вашего письма не предназначены для публикации, хотя мы в любом случае всегда действуем на свое усмотрение. Письма также могут быть отредактированы для ясности и сокращены... Пожалуйста, напишите, если вы не против прямой переписки с другими читателями OUTLET, и мы опубликуем ваш полный адрес.

Вторая проблема: как сохранить (SAVE) подпрограмму из OUTLET, чтобы использовать её в собственных программах?

### Ответ Kenneth Hunter от Brian

Обычно любую программу целиком из OUTLET можно сохранить с помощью `RUN 9982` (использование `RUN` вместо `GO TO` очищает переменные и экономит место на диске). Впрочем, в уже существующих программах сначала проверьте строку, так как изредка по разным причинам мне приходилось использовать другую строку (часто 8982). Однако сейчас я стараюсь стандартизировать строку 9982, а для кассет — 9983. Строка 9980 содержит опцию ERASE для тех, кто хочет сначала стереть более раннюю версию. Обычно я НЕ рекомендую перезаписывать программу обратно на диск или картридж OUTLET — лучше сделайте новую рабочую копию (если только вы не сделали полную резервную копию всего выпуска OUTLET!).

Отдельные подпрограммы, которые подробно описаны в программе, почти всегда можно извлечь следующим образом:

1. Нажмите `E` на титульной странице, чтобы стереть (ERASE) остальной BASIC.
2. Введите `SAVE ... "ANYNAME"` (НЕ добавляйте номер строки автозапуска после имени).
3. Загрузите (LOAD) свою программу, в которой вы хотите использовать подпрограмму.
4. Введите `MERGE ... "ANYNAME"`.
5. Затем следуйте инструкциям из программы OUTLET, но чаще всего это будет просто `GO SUB 1234` (или любой другой указанный номер строки).

Эту команду `GO SUB` обычно следует помещать в строку ближе к началу вашей программы (после загрузки). Всегда следуйте инструкциям в программе OUTLET. Часто в случае машинного кода, хранящегося в операторах REM, перед `GO SUB` вам потребуется добавить в программу оператор `CLEAR`, чтобы сдвинуть RAMTOP ниже начального адреса кода. Проверьте работоспособность программы и затем сохраните её заново.

Чтобы использовать подпрограмму, которая просто случайно оказалась внутри программы OUTLET (то есть не является основной темой программы), вам придётся удалить остальной BASIC либо построчно (!), либо с помощью подпрограммы блочного удаления. (Одна из таких, DELINER, есть в Выпуске 5).

Пожалуйста, напишите нам, если возникнут конкретные проблемы.

В настоящее время я пытаюсь упорядочить и стандартизировать опции печати, используемые в OUTLET. Предусмотреть поддержку абсолютно всех интерфейсов невозможно, поэтому мы охватываем основные из них, и я хочу добавить пункт "USER'S OWN", чтобы каждый мог с помощью MERGE добавить собственную процедуру. Я стараюсь придерживаться одних и тех же номеров строк, но это нелегко.

Как правило, вам нужно прервать программу клавишей BREAK, дать команду LIST в районе строк 9700–9800 и изменить одну из существующих строк настройки интерфейса под вашу систему. В большинстве программ строка 9888 (которая в настоящее время содержит `LPRINT III`) инициализирует принтер для вывода текста, а в строке 9895 задаются начальные управляющие коды, такие как настройки полей. Процедуры дампа графики высокого разрешения находятся в районе строк 9782 и 9786. Программа оглавления CONTENTS BASIC (а также TEXT LOADER для пользователей магнитофона) сейчас устроена иначе. Посмотрите строку 1356. В целях экономии места коды в этой строке «встроены» в текстовую строку, но вы можете просто удалить их и вставить свои. Надеюсь, я приведу CONTENTS к общему стандарту с другими программами OUTLET, но на данный момент я всё ещё собираю информацию. Одна проблема заключается в том, что некоторым принтерам требуется код перевода строки (line feed), а некоторым нет. Другая проблема — текст CONTENTS может быть полностью переписан.

В вашем конкретном случае, как мне подсказали, вам нужно инициализировать интерфейс принтера следующим образом:

```text
FORMAT "P"; 1200 (или любая скорость,
                  на которую настроен
                  ваш принтер)
OPEN #3;"P"

POKE 23349,39: POKE 23350,1
  (перед отправкой управляющих кодов)
```

Вам, вероятно, придётся немного поэкспериментировать, чтобы всё заработало, но пишите нам снова, если у вас возникнут сложности с конкретными программами. Жаль, что не могу помочь сильнее, но каждая программа индивидуальна и может немного отличаться, к тому же у меня самого нет +2, так что я не могу ничего проверить наверняка. Другие читатели OUTLET, использующие +2, возможно, смогут посоветовать вам что-то получше, так что напишите ещё раз, если зайдёте в тупик.

— Brian.
